7. Per contra, Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 made sub-missions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He has submitted that, the Waqif Azizur Rahman of Waqf Deed No.5303 registered on 15.11.1928 (E.C. 1690 of 1935) was also the Executive Mutawalli (Mutawalli No.2) of Waqf Deed No.1402, registered on 22.03.1928, (E.C. 2059 of 1937), therein the Waqif Abdul Gani admitted and it is apparent on the face of ; the Deed itself and both the Waqifs had knowledge about the same and there was no conflict or inconsistency in between both the Waqf Deeds as Abdul Gani had rent receiving interest on schedule 11 whereas Azizur Rahman was the tenant and became tenant by registered Kabuliat dated 20.07.1917 and 13.05.1926 of the same schedule as evident from R.S. Khatian Nos. Nos.1236, 1237, 1238 and 1239, and, that position having been maintained, and, valid till coming into operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by which the rent receiving interest of Taluk by Abdul Gani or his Waqf had stood acquired in the name of the Government and, hence, the land of the Waqf Deed No.1402 dated 22.03.1928 in particular schedule 11 in which Waqif Abdul Gani had rent receiving interest had ; acquired and ceased from the schedule of the said Deed by operation of law. On the contrary no record of rights in favour of the Waqf of E.C. 2059 after acquisition of rent receiving interest by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and, therefore, the Waqf Administrator have no jurisdiction under section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance to declare title in favour of Waqf Deed No.1402 by deleting the properties from Waqf Deed No.5303 dated 30.09.2007 after 79 years. He has finally submitted that, Title Suit No.53 of 1945 filed by the predecessor of the appellant, the then Mutawalli Rahimunnessa of E.C. No.2059 made Azizur Rahman, the then Mutawalli of E.C. No. 1690 as proforma defendant No.5 wherein she admitted the Waqf Deed and its E.C. No.1690 and Azizur Rahman as tenant (খাস দখলীয় রায়ত স্তিতিবান) praying for decree of Taluka title though her tenant (কায়েমী প্রজা) the defendant No.5, wherein, she got decree on 31.07.1946 heard and disposed of analogous with Rent Suit No.72 of 1945, wherein, both Azizur Rahman and Rahimunnessa as defendant Nos.1 and 2 respectively and, as such, the High Court Division was correct in holding that the respondent No.2, the Administrator of Waqfs who was respondent No.1, in writ petition "fallen in misconception of law and passed the impugned order on finding of law that "since the deeds are registered on, in respect of the property maintained in one schedule cannot be treated in another schedule of the deeds and, as such, the High court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order. Hence, therefore, he prays for dismissal the instant appeal. 

 24.
